ai.description: The Nilgiri Day Gecko (Gekkonidae) reaches 45 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow-spotted vertebral stripe and a white-tipped tail. Key features include granular scales and smooth ventrals.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Nilgiri Day Gecko is best identified by the distinct, continuous row of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along its flanks, which are absent in most other regional congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis nilagirica* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Nilgiri Hills, typically found on tree trunks and rocky surfaces at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.behavior: The Nilgiri Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis nilagirica* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nilgiri Day Gecko is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting the Nilgiri Hills in Tamil Nadu and Kerala at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
